title: Mailgun Prefix-less 32-8-8 hex key triplet, Mailgun Private API key and HTTP webhook signing key and 1 more: must be flagged
summary: Synthetic Mailgun Prefix-less 32-8-8 hex key triplet, Mailgun Private API key and HTTP webhook signing key and 1 more values built to the documented format appear in 12 inputs across 10 carrier types. Each input records the exact byte range of the secret.
rationale: A credential that a scanner misses in an ordinary carrier is leaked. Carriers differ in quoting, delimiters and surrounding text, so a hit on one carrier does not show coverage of another.

expectation.rationale: Context-gated arrival family (#259, product redact-secret#701). Three sources describe a prefix-less <32 hex>-<8 hex>-<8 hex> value as Mailgun's newer private API key: a Mailgun-repository contributor (mailgun-go#72, 2019), customer reports (Discourse, 2018) and trufflehog#3870 (2025). Both pinned peers match the shape: gitleaks 8.30.1 mailgun-signing-key (keyword-gated, [a-h0-9]) and trufflehog 3.97.4 mailgun (its "Hex MailGun Token" pattern, chunk-keyword-gated). Mailgun documents no shape for any key, so no issued key is known and the contract is recorded uncertainty. Before this issue, the benchmark taxonomy listed the triplet as an unsupported legacy signing key; this issue corrects that reason. The triplet is recognised only beside a same-line mailgun keyword and scores as policy. Its twins keep the triplet and change only the context. The alphabet is lowercase hex, the intersection of both peers, so an uppercase triplet is a near-miss control rather than a twin.
